question: The Vice President of India can be removed from office by__________.

options.text: Resolution passed by the Council of States and agreed to by the House of the People
Resolution passed by both Houses of Parliament with one-thirds majority
The President on the advice of the Prime Minister

solution:
The correct answer is __**Resolution passed by the Council of States and agreed to by the House of the People**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 

• **Article 67** of the Constitution of India states that the **Vice President of India** can be removed from office through a **resolution passed by the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and agreed to by the House of the People (Lok Sabha).** 

• The resolution must be passed in the **Rajya Sabha by an absolute majority** (more than half of the total members) and then agreed to by the **Lok Sabha.** 

• The process for removal requires the resolution to be introduced after a **14-day prior notice** signed by at least 50 members of the Rajya Sabha. 

• This provision ensures that the removal of the Vice President is conducted with due deliberation, maintaining the dignity of the office. 

• The Vice President can only be removed for reasons that align with the rules and procedures of parliamentary democracy; arbitrary removal is not permitted. *Hence, the correct answer is Resolution passed by the Council of States and agreed to by the House of the People.* 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **Role of the Vice President:** 
 

• The Vice President of India is the **ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha**. 

• He/she acts as the second-highest constitutional office in India and assists the President in case of absence or resignation. 

• The term of the Vice President is **five years**, but he/she can continue in office until the successor assumes charge. 
 
 

• **Election Process:** 
 

• The Vice President is elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the **members of both Houses of Parliament**. 

• The election is conducted through a **single transferable vote system** and is by secret ballot. 

• The candidate must be a citizen of India, at least **35 years old**, and qualified to be a member of the Rajya Sabha. 
 
 

• **Removal Procedure:** 
 

• The Vice President can be removed through a resolution passed in the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha, as per **Article 67**. 

• A **14-day notice** is mandatory before moving the resolution. 

• Unlike the President, the Vice President does not face impeachment; the removal process is simpler but requires legislative consensus. 
 
 

• **Important Articles:** 
 

• **Article 63:** Specifies that there shall be a Vice President of India. 

• **Article 64:** States the role of the Vice President as the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. 

• **Article 66:** Deals with the election of the Vice President. 

• **Article 67:** Provides for the removal of the Vice President. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Comparison with Presidential Impeachment:** 
 

• The **President** of India can be removed through an impeachment process, which is more complex and requires charges to be proved. 

• The **Vice President**, however, is removed through a resolution, making the process less rigorous. 
 
 

• **Historical Context:** 
 

• Since the establishment of the office, no Vice President of India has been removed from office. 

• This reflects the stability of the constitutional framework and the respect for the office. 
 
 

• **Significance of the Office:** 
 

• The Vice President ensures the smooth functioning of the Rajya Sabha and acts as a crucial link in legislative processes. 

• He/she plays a key role in maintaining parliamentary decorum and resolving disputes within the Rajya Sabha.
